<wait>When you dig through mythology and legend, you notice - and it's
quite startling - one particular motif that shows up over and
over again. That motif is "incest."

<wait>Japanese myth, and then Greek myth, and the Old Testament to
name a few - across the myths of every region of the world, this
motif is embedded as though it were the common standard of the
mythic world.

<wait>What's more, incest within myth represents nothing less than
the world, the cosmos itself, and, at times, plays the role of
giving rise to the crucial elements that make up humanity and
the systems of culture.

<wait>So what exactly is this "incest" that so often carries such
important meaning and role within this mythic world......?
